hints: Look carefully at the diagram and notice which wall layer X is pointing to. Is it the very thin inner lining, the thick middle ring, or the thin outer coat?
Remember what the thick tunica media of an artery is built to do (stretch, recoil and constrict) and which three tissues allow it to do that.
walkthrough:
**Identify layer X**

Look at the transverse section. You can see a small central lumen, then a very thick middle wall, then a thinner outer coat. The label X is pointing to that thick middle ring.

That thick middle ring is the tunica media.

**Recall what the tunica media contains**

Arteries carry blood at high pressure straight from the heart. So the tunica media needs to be strong, stretchy and able to contract.

To do this it contains smooth muscle (to contract and control diameter), elastic fibres (to stretch and recoil with each pulse) and collagen (for tensile strength to prevent bursting).

**Choose the matching statement**

Since layer X is the tunica media, it must contain all three tissues together. That matches only option D.

options.A: This misses out elastic fibres, which are essential in the arterial tunica media for stretching and recoiling with blood pressure.
options.B: This misses out smooth muscle, which is a major part of the tunica media for vasoconstriction and control of blood flow.
options.C: This misses out collagen, which is needed in the tunica media for strength to resist high pressure and prevent the wall tearing.
options.D: Correct. Layer X is the tunica media of the artery, which contains smooth muscle, elastic fibres and collagen together.
